description: Hands-on lab covering makefiles, gcc/clang usage, code debugging with gdb, profiling and optimization with gprof, memory management using valgrind, version control systems, Unix commands and shell scripting, linking/loading programs and ELF analysis, and system configuration and management.

Advanced algorithmic paradigms including divide and conquer, dynamic programming, greedy, branch and bound, randomized algorithms, geometric, algebraic and graph algorithms, NP-completeness, approximation algorithms, and introduction to external memory and parallel algorithms.

Study of CPU, memory, and I/O subsystems, instruction set architecture, data representation, computer arithmetic, CPU control unit design, memory system design, peripheral devices, interrupts, and performance enhancement techniques including pipelining and cache memory organization.

Design and implementation of compilers for imperative languages, covering lexical analysis, syntax and semantic analysis, symbol tables, runtime environment, intermediate code generation, code optimization, register allocation, target code generation, and advanced topics like type systems and OOP compilation.
Hands-on lab on database schema design, SQL programming, report generation using commercial RDBMS, front-end tools, ODBC/CORBA calls, internet-based database access, and database administration.

Introduction to operating systems including processes, scheduling, context switching, process synchronization, threads, deadlocks, memory management (contiguous, non-contiguous, paging, virtual memory), file systems, disk and I/O management, virtualization, and case studies.

Hands-on lab to familiarize with UNIX system calls for process management and inter-process communication; experiments on process scheduling and other OS tasks via simulation or implementation using environments like Nachos.

Study of computability and complexity theory, including Turing machines, undecidability, primitive recursive and mu-recursive functions, lambda calculus, oracle machines, arithmetic hierarchy, time/space complexity, reductions, logic, and quantified Boolean formulas.

Covers logic families (TTL, CMOS, etc.), Boolean algebra, switching functions, combinational and sequential circuits, minimization techniques (K-map, Quine-McCluskey, BDD), circuit synthesis with ROMs/PLAs/FPGAs, and ASM chart-based sequential circuit design.

Lab on requirements specification, function-oriented design using SA/SD, object-oriented design using UML, test case design, implementation in Java, and software life cycle tools including CASE and configuration management.

Hands-on lab for pulse circuits (bistable, astable, monostable), TTL and CMOS gates, combinational circuits like ALU and 7-segment drivers, sequential circuits including counters and ASM designs (e.g., traffic light controllers).

Lab focusing on implementation and analysis of algorithms from class, use of various data structures, comparison of algorithmic approaches, and design of algorithms for new problems, including a large-scale project using multiple algorithms and data structures.

Introduction to asymptotic notations, RAM model, complexity analysis, basic algorithmic paradigms, searching and sorting algorithms, priority queues, heaps, trees, string matching, and fundamental graph algorithms like BFS, DFS, MST, and shortest paths.

Covers propositional logic, proof techniques, sets, relations and functions, counting principles, recurrence relations, algebraic structures (semigroups, monoids, groups, rings, fields), Boolean algebra, and introductory graph theory including trees, Eulerian/Hamiltonian walks, and graph coloring.

Study of alphabets, languages, grammars, regular and context-free languages, finite automata (DFA/NFA), pushdown automata, context-sensitive languages, Turing machines, undecidability, Church-Turing thesis, universal Turing machine, and reductions between languages.
